newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican prison head quits amid jailbreaks, scandals.
newsitem.headline: Mexican prison head quits amid jailbreaks, scandals.

text.p: The head of Mexico City's prison system quit on Tuesday amid a scandal over luxuries enjoyed by a few privileged inmates, as well as a spate of bloody jailbreaks in recent months.

Raul Gutierrez, director general of prisons, had been under criticism for weeks, especially after armed convicts shot their way out of the front gates of the Reclusorio del Oriente prison in a bloody gunbattle in which two died in March.
It was the latest of a series of prison breakouts under Gutierrez's tenure, during which Televisa television said 33 convicts had managed to escape.
More recently, the Mexico City Human Rights Office presented photographic evidence to city councillors of gaping inequalities between rich and poor convicts in some of the city's toughest jails.

According to head of the human rights office, Luis de la Barrera, some of the richest inmates in the maximum-security wing of the Reclusorio Norte prison have several cells to themselves, matrimonial-size beds, CD players, a private gym and varnished cupboards stocked with imported foods.
Their less fortunate counterparts are forced to crowd up to 29 to a cell, using newspapers to keep warm, sleeping on matresses or cardboard boxes on the floor and eating foul food, he said.

Photographs in Reforma newspaper on Tuesday contrasted filthy toilets and cooking areas used by the majority of inmates with the sparkling clean kitchens and bathrooms of the privileged, who reportedly include major drug traffickers.
The office of Mexico City Mayor Oscar Espinosa said he had accepted Gutierrez's resignation.
